A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OSCAR despite the changed title. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support reliable matching of retained, relocated and revised material.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation experiments, toy simulations, safeguard ablations and noise-sensitivity results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and reports additional compositional-prompt, ImageNet, computational-budget and robustness evaluations.

M1.justification: The feature-volume objective, orthogonal control and redundancy reweighting remain central. The stated numerical procedure changes from Heun extrapolation and predictor-corrector updates to finite-difference endpoints and a single controlled update; Equation 3 also drops the trace stabilizer. Since v1 already named an Euler scheduler, these revisions do not establish that retained experiments used a newly implemented sampler.

E1.justification: v2 adds T2I-CompBench spatial-color and complex prompts, evaluation on 400 ImageNet classes, additional COCO concepts including apple, suitcase and pizza, and challenging portrait examples. These substantially broaden the evaluated content and compositional requirements beyond v1's retained COCO and toy settings.

E2.justification: v2 adds FM-SD3.5 and APG to the main truck comparison, and FM-SD3.5 to the bus and bicycle comparisons. Mix ODE/SDE is additionally evaluated in diagnostic and small-batch comparisons. PG, CADS and DPP/DiverseFlow remain existing comparators.

E3.justification: v2 adds KID, CLIP-IQA, ImageReward and BLIPVQA evaluation, compute-matched controls, small-batch tests and alternative backbone/encoder settings. The safeguard ablation changes from CFG 3.0 to 5.0, and the default gate endpoint changes from 0.35 to 0.40. The new CompBench protocol is internally inconsistent: Section 5.1 specifies 100 prompts per subset and 16 images per prompt, whereas Appendix C.5 specifies 300 prompts and 32 images.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's separate safeguard ablations and noise/NFE sweeps, v2 adds joint safeguard removal, predictor and encoder ablations, backbone transfer, small-batch robustness, compute-matched comparisons and mixed-sampler diagnostics. It also adds prompt-level and particle-density analyses. Existing toy plots and noise sweeps are partly relocated rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: v1 already reports aggregation over at least four seeds and standard-deviation bands. v2 additionally specifies six seeds and mean plus or minus 95% confidence intervals for the predictor, backbone and encoder studies in Tables 19-21. This does not establish increased repetition of the retained experiments.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive results for new tasks, comparators, metrics and analyses, and replaces some retained results. For example, Table 1's OSCAR truck FID at CFG 3.0 changes from 126.35 ± 0.59 to 165.40 ± 0.94; truck, bus and bicycle PRD curves also change. Many original diversity scores and noise-sweep values remain identical. Unreconciled procedure/settings descriptions prevent attributing these replacements to same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Appendix B expands v1's statements and sketches with proofs concerning pullback, energy descent, volume and noise-budget bounds. It also introduces a Girsanov path-measure/KL theorem and a process-level coupling bound, absent from v1. The inherited noise-budget corollary is reformulated and elaborated, rather than wholly new.

C1.justification: The central claim of training-free diversity enhancement with fidelity preservation remains. v2 removes the abstract's explicit claim of requiring no base-sampler modification and compatibility with common solvers, while expanding the conclusion to propose OSCAR as complementary to RL post-training and a possible exploration prior.

C2.justification: v2 adds explicit limitations concerning jointly active trajectories, strict one-image-per-prompt use and inference overhead in Appendix G. It also explains the support-coverage versus density-matching trade-off at high particle counts, prompt-induced metric variability and the limitations of unconstrained stochastic exploration. These materially qualify and extend v1's interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 supplies the finite-difference predictor formula, concrete CADS and DiverseFlow configurations, additional evaluator/reference-set details, and measured FLOPs, runtime and VRAM with hardware information. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation. However, the OSCAR repository link supplied in v1's abstract is removed; this establishes loss of the access pointer, not that the repository became unavailable.

R1.justification: The existing diffusion, flow and diversity-method positioning largely remains. v2 adds a substantive distinction from APG and discusses complementarity with RL post-training, including new MixGRPO and DanceGRPO citations. Additional references support the new benchmarks, metrics and backbone studies.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title, author information and several headings, revises the abstract and introduction, separates sensitivity analysis, and expands the concluding discussion. Appendix organization and disclosures change, but much original prose and the overall main-section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text is reformatted from a single-column preprint to a two-column conference layout. Figure 1 is rearranged, existing toy plots and galleries are relocated, the combined parameter figure is split into a table and visual figure, and comparison tables gain rows and metric blocks. Numerous new experimental tables and qualitative panels substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The added base-model/APG controls, compute-matched comparisons, targeted robustness tests and explicit limitations address important evidential gaps in v1. The net benefit is limited by conflicting CompBench sample counts, unexplained truck FID replacements, and cross-backbone claims of no quality degradation that conflict with Table 20. The paper becomes more assessable, but the expanded conclusions still require substantial qualification.
